lesson.title: Messy names, wrong counts
lesson.subtitle: Exact matches, cleaning in steps, and strip and lower in Python

video.title: Messy names, wrong counts
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma — the maths teacher (main character)
Mr Joseph — the computer studies teacher (cameo)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: An online vote; 3 places?; The same zoo!. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your class voted online for the school trip. The computer counted “Zoo”, “zoo” and “the zoo” as three different places. It's the same zoo!

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: messy text that breaks counts, and how to clean it.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A space at the end; A capital letter; One different letter; People: one. Computer: three.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Computers compare text exactly, letter by letter. A space at the end, a capital letter or one different letter makes a new answer. People see one word; the computer sees three.

scenes.visual: Numbered steps: Remove the end spaces; Make the letters match; Match a list of answers.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Clean in steps. First, remove the spaces at the ends. Next, make the letters match: all small in English, one form of each Arabic letter. Last, match each answer to a list of allowed answers.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A list to choose from; Not a box to type in; Nothing to clean.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Better still, stop it happening. Give people a list to choose from, not a box to type in. A drop-down list means nothing to clean.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! To a computer, is a word with a space at the end the same as the word without it?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: “zoo␣” ≠ “zoo”; First: trim the spaces.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A space is a character too
scenes.narration: No: the space is a character too, so it's a different answer. That's why cleaning starts by removing the spaces at the ends.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: votes = [" Zoo", "zoo", "ZOO "] … Caption: Prints ['zoo', 'zoo', 'zoo']
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Python can clean text for you. strip removes the spaces at both ends. lower makes every letter small. Do it in a loop, and every answer gets the same treatment.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Before: 3 places; Clean; After: 1 place, 9 votes.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Count again after cleaning. Before: three different places. After: one place, with all nine votes. Same votes, the right answer.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: 20 names; Tidied: 13; Matched: 8.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, two teachers typed a week's register. Tidy the names, then match them to the class list. Watch the names counted go from twenty to thirteen, and then to eight.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Which of these stops messy answers before they even start?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Compared exactly; Spaces, letters, then a list; A drop-down prevents it; strip() and lower(). Takeaway bar: Clean text, then count: the right answer.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A drop-down list: nobody types, so nothing gets messy. Remember: computers compare text exactly. Clean in steps: spaces, letters, then a list. And in Python, strip and lower do the tidying.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A sign-up sheet or poll; How many ways?; Write the clean list. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: look at a sign-up sheet, or a class poll where people typed their answers. Count how many ways one answer was written. Then write the clean list.

checkpoints.prompt: To a computer, is a word with a space at the end the same as the word without it?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a space is a character, so the computer sees a different word. Strip the spaces first.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a computer compares every character, spaces included, in any language.

checkpoints.prompt: Which of these stops messy answers before they start?

options.text: A drop-down list to choose from

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — when people choose instead of typing, every answer is written the same way.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — any typing box lets new spellings in. A drop-down list means people choose, so nothing gets messy.
